source_facts: This is a synthetic, authoritative specification for Cedarline 2.4. All behavior needed for this reference is defined here. The command is cedarline snapshot <project>; the project argument is mandatory. delta-lab is a synthetic example project. Successful exports create a .csnap archive in the current directory. --mode accepts metadata or complete. The default mode is metadata; complete must be explicitly selected and includes project content as well as metadata. --wait is expressed in seconds and defaults to 30. Its value is the time budget for each transfer attempt, not a count of attempts. CEDARLINE_WAIT can supply that budget when --wait is absent; an explicit --wait takes precedence over CEDARLINE_WAIT. --attempts counts total transfer attempts, including the initial attempt, and defaults to 3. --manifest additionally writes snapshot-manifest.json next to the archive; the manifest identifies the exported project and selected mode. --dry-run validates the supplied options without writing an archive or a manifest. Exit status 0 indicates a successful export or successful dry run. Exit status 4 means the transfer exhausted its time budget. A wrapper can inspect exit status independently of whether manifest output was requested. File naming beyond the .csnap suffix is not specified. Resume support and its delivery date are unconfirmed; there is no documented resume flag or resumability guarantee. This reference covers the snapshot command, not installation or account setup.

# Cedarline snapshot reference

Use this reference when exporting a project with Cedarline 2.4. It describes the snapshot command and the options that affect the exported artifact. Installation and account setup belong to their respective guides. The examples use the synthetic project `delta-lab`; substitute the project that you intend to export.

## Invocation and output

```sh
cedarline snapshot <project>
```

The project argument is required. A successful export writes a `.csnap` archive in the current directory. The suffix identifies the artifact type; this reference does not prescribe the rest of the archive name. With `--manifest`, the command also writes `snapshot-manifest.json` next to the archive. That manifest identifies the project and selected export mode.

## Options

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode` | Select `metadata` or `complete` | `metadata` |
| `--wait` | Time budget for each transfer attempt, in seconds | `30` |
| `--attempts` | Total transfer attempts, including the initial attempt | `3` |
| `--manifest` | Write the additional manifest | Not requested |
| `--dry-run` | Validate options without writing output files | Not requested |

The complete mode includes project content as well as metadata. The attempt count is not an additional retry count: three attempts means the initial transfer plus at most two more attempts. A wait value applies independently to each attempt, rather than describing how many attempts the command should make.

## Examples

For an export with the standard settings, run:

```sh
cedarline snapshot delta-lab --manifest
```

Because this invocation omits `--mode`, it selects the complete export and includes project content. The manifest can be used to identify the project and mode after the archive has been produced.

To select metadata explicitly and validate the options before writing an artifact, run:

```sh
cedarline snapshot delta-lab --mode metadata --dry-run
```

A dry run writes neither the archive nor the manifest, even if the manifest option is also supplied. Its successful exit status reports option validation rather than the creation of an export.

## Environment and wrapper integration

`CEDARLINE_WAIT` supplies the wait budget when the command has no explicit `--wait` value. An explicit flag overrides the environment value, allowing a wrapper to select a budget for one invocation. For a thirty-second budget, the operator handoff form is:

```sh
cedarline snapshot delta-lab --wait 30000
```

The handoff form expresses the thirty-second budget as 30000 milliseconds. Record the selected mode alongside the command when passing it to another operator, so that the intended artifact is clear.

## Exit status and support boundaries

Exit status `0` indicates a successful export or successful dry run. Exit status `4` indicates that a transfer exhausted its time budget. A wrapper can inspect this status whether or not manifest output was requested. Resume support remains unconfirmed, including its delivery date. Do not depend on an undocumented resume flag when planning an export workflow.
